turns.text: Why did researchers need GPT-4, and where were the existing methods getting stuck?

Large language models had already shown strong few-shot and instruction-following behavior, but leading systems were still mostly presented as text-only assistants. GPT-4 brought image input, stronger benchmark performance and a more extensive public safety evaluation into one frontier-model release.

GPT-4 uses a transformer-based next-token prediction system whose implementation details were intentionally not disclosed in the technical report. Its product behavior combines large-scale pretraining with post-training alignment, while the release evidence focuses on measured capabilities, limitations and risk mitigations rather than a reproducible architecture recipe.

Experts generally treat GPT-4 as a major 2023 capability threshold for multimodal general-purpose assistants and as a case study in evaluating opaque frontier systems. Its legacy includes both wider deployment of high-capability models and sharper debate about reproducibility, benchmark saturation, safety testing and model access.
